The Platform

3

What is NRP?

  • A national Kubernetes cluster, Nautilus, for research and education
  • Run by SDSC (UC San Diego), Nebraska–Lincoln and MGHPCC; funded by NSF
  • Hardware contributed by 70+ institutions, UCLA among them
  • Scale today:
  • 536 nodes
  • 1,411 GPUs in 33 models
  • Petabytes of storage
  • Free for non-commercial research and education
https://dash.nrp-nautilus.io

Site locations from the NRP dashboard, 10 Nov 2026
Not drawn: 8 sites in Hawaii, Guam, Korea, Brazil and Europe

4

Kubernetes and Containers

  • Container image: your code plus everything it needs (Python, PyTorch, CUDA), in one package
  • Runs the same on a laptop, a cluster or the cloud
  • Kubernetes runs containers across many machines
  • You say what you need (CPUs, memory, a GPU); it finds a machine that has it
  • NRP is one Kubernetes cluster: 536 nodes

What NRP Is For

Public or synthetic data

public datasets, simulations, benchmark and synthetic data

De-identified data

if your IRB and data use agreement allow it

Protected health information

PHI or identifiable patient data, including in LLM prompts

OK on NRP
Not on NRP

Good uses

model development and training · image analysis · simulation · teaching · LLMs on non-sensitive text

Also not for: commercial work, or services that need guaranteed uptime (it is a shared, best-effort cluster)

NRP is not HIPAA compliant. Keep PHI in UCLA Health's approved environments.

Getting Access

1.  Log in at nrp.ai

Log In → CILogon → choose UCLA → your UCLA login

2.  Get into a namespace

Request one at get-started.nrp-nautilus.io
Or ask an existing namespace admin to add you

3.  Start working

JupyterHub, kubectl, or an LLM token from nrp.ai/llmtoken

Who can request a namespace: faculty, staff, postdocs and research scientists. Students: your PI or instructor requests it and adds you.

https://get-started.nrp-nautilus.io
9

What is a Namespace?

  • Your group's workspace on the cluster
  • One per lab, project or course; the PI or instructor is its admin and adds members
  • Needed for GPU jobs, storage, your own JupyterHub, and API access to the hosted LLMs
  • Not needed to chat with the LLMs in the browser
  • What's inside is visible only to its members

GPUs on NRP

  • 1,411 GPUs in 33 models, contributed by campuses
  • Most common: A10 and RTX 3090, 24 GB each

Choosing a GPU

GPU memoryExamplesGood forHow to ask
Up to 16 GBRTX 2080 Ti, GTX 1080 Ti, A4000, A100 slicesTeaching, debugging, classic ML, small CNNsnvidia.com/gpu: 1
20–24 GBA10, RTX 3090, L4, RTX 4090Most deep learning; fine-tuning and serving models up to ~8B parametersnvidia.com/gpu: 1 + memory or model
32–48 GBL40, V100 32 GB, RTX A6000, A40Bigger models and batches; serving models up to ~30Bnvidia.com/gpu, or rtxa6000 / a40
80 GB and upA100 80 GB, H100, H200Large training runs and large modelsA100: access request; H100/H200 reserved

Current PyTorch builds need Turing or newer: on a GTX 1080 Ti or V100, use an older image.

14

Ways to Run Work

Interactive: JupyterHub

  • Pick a GPU from the start menu; explore, debug, teach
  • Idle servers stop: 1 hour after you close the browser on NRP's hub, 6 hours at most on any hub

Interactive: a pod

  • Start a container with kubectl, then open a shell in it
  • Deleted after 6 hours; at most 2 GPUs

Long-running: a Deployment

  • Keeps a service up (a web app, a database) and restarts it if it crashes
  • Removed after 2 weeks unless admins grant an exception; no GPU if it sits mostly idle

Batch: a Job

  • Runs your script to the end, then gives the GPU back
  • Submit many at once; the rest wait in Pending for a free GPU
$ kubectl apply -f sweep/        # six training jobs
Pendinglr-0.1lr-0.03lr-0.01lr-0.003lr-0.001lr-0.0003GPU 1GPU 2GPU 3GPU 4lr-0.1lr-0.03lr-0.01lr-0.003lr-0.001lr-0.0003time

Six jobs on four GPUs: two wait in Pending and take the first GPUs that free up. When the last one ends, all four GPUs are free again.

15

A GPU Job

apiVersion: batch/v1kind: Jobmetadata: {name: gpu-train-daniel, namespace: my-lab}     # (1)spec:  template:    spec:      restartPolicy: Never      containers:      - name: train        image: pytorch/pytorch:2.9.0-cuda13.0-cudnn9-runtime  # (2)        command: ["python", "train.py"]        resources:                                       # (3)          requests: {cpu: "2", memory: 6Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: 1}          limits:   {cpu: "2", memory: 6Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: 1}      affinity:                                          # (4)        nodeAffinity:          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:            nodeSelectorTerms:            - matchExpressions:              - {key: nvidia.com/gpu.memory, operator: Gt, values: ["20000"]}              - {key: nvidia.com/gpu.compute.major, operator: Gt, values: ["7"]}

(1) Where: your namespace

(2) What: a container image, and the command to run

(3) Resources: 2 CPUs, 6 GB of memory, one GPU

(4) Which GPU: more than 20 GB, Ampere or newer; or name exact models

16

Running the Job

# submitkubectl apply -f gpu-job.yaml # watch: Pending → Running → Completedkubectl get pods -l job-name=gpu-train-daniel # read the outputkubectl logs -f job/gpu-train-daniel # clean upkubectl delete job gpu-train-daniel

Stuck in Pending? kubectl describe pod says why, usually that no matching GPU is free.

Our test: under 30 s from submit to done on an A10 that had the image; several minutes in Pending when the cluster was full.

Output, 9 Nov 2026
Running on: NVIDIA A10Matrix multiply, 4096 x 4096:  CPU (2 cores)  0.09 TFLOP/s  GPU            14.0 TFLOP/s  (154x)Training on 60,000 images, testing on 10,000epoch 1: loss 0.090, accuracy 98.4%, 1.6 sepoch 2: loss 0.009, accuracy 98.7%, 1.0 sepoch 3: loss 0.033, accuracy 98.7%, 1.1 sDone: the job exits and frees the GPU.
17

Using GPUs Fairly

Do

  • Run batch work as a Job that exits
  • Request what you'll use; keep limits within 20% of requests
  • Keep data on a persistent volume or in S3
  • Run a sweep as many one-GPU jobs
  • Borrow idle A100/H100s with priorityClassName: opportunistic, and checkpoint

Don't

  • Leave a notebook holding a GPU overnight
  • Put sleep in a Job to keep a GPU (bannable)
  • Ask for 4 GPUs "just in case": use must stay above 40%
  • Keep results on the pod's own disk; it vanishes with the pod
https://nrp.ai/documentation/userdocs/start/policies/

AI Services

19

Hosted LLMs

  • Open-weight models on NRP GPUs, behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint:
  • ellm.nrp-nautilus.io/v1
  • Free for non-commercial research and education
  • Prompts are processed on NRP hardware, not sent to a commercial provider
  • Still not for PHI
  • About 7.1 billion tokens a day (September 2026)
ModelGood for
qwen3, qwen3-smallHard reasoning, long documents, images
gpt-ossGeneral chat, reproducible research
glm-5, kimi, minimaxAgentic coding
deepseek-v4-flashWhole codebases, very long documents
gemma, gemma-smallImages, video, audio transcription
qwen3-embeddingSearch and RAG (embeddings)
https://nrp.ai/documentation/userdocs/ai/llm-managed/models/

Uses from the models page, 26 Oct 2026. The catalog rotates.

Using the LLMs

Claude Code on NRP's gpt-oss, asked about the demo's GPU job

21

Jupyter AI

  • Already pointed at NRP's models on the training hub, and on any course hub you run
  • Chat panel: ask about code, an error or a concept
  • /fix: select a cell that crashed; it explains and proposes a fix
  • %%ai magics: {variables} in a prompt become their live values, so the model sees your data
%%ai openai-chat:gpt-ossHere is a summary of my dataset: {summary}Which columns would you check first, and why?
22

Running Your Own Models

  • Serve your own model: vLLM or SGLang on a GPU in your namespace, your weights or your fine-tune behind the same OpenAI API; ask the admins before running one as a long-lived service
  • Train and fine-tune: PyTorch and Hugging Face in GPU jobs, from one GPU to eight on a node
  • Search your documents (RAG): qwen3-embedding and NRP's managed Milvus vector database
  • Inference accelerators: Qualcomm Cloud AI 100 cards, requested in a job like a GPU

Worked examples: the PEARC26 tutorial (serving, RAG), and a physics neural network trained in GPU jobs (CMS HATS)

https://training.nrp-nautilus.io
